consensus_summary: Primary symbolic meaning is spiritual/covenant unfaithfulness to God (chiefly idolatry and apostasy), grounded in the marriage metaphor; political alliances, worldly compromise, and specific historical referents appear as common extensions or secondary applications, while literal sexual immorality remains the non-symbolic base sense.
book_summary: Covenant unfaithfulness consisting in joining oneself to other gods or kingdoms outside the union God established; the physical sexual sin supplies the image.
consensus_core_identification: covenant/spiritual unfaithfulness to God (idolatry/apostasy) imaged as sexual infidelity
book_core_identification: covenant unfaithfulness (joining other gods or kingdoms) with physical sin as the image
rationale: Both reduce to the identical core referent: covenant breach against God imaged by sexual unfaithfulness. The book’s explicit inclusion of “kingdoms” alongside “gods” simply restates the political-alliance extension already treated as common or included within the consensus primary meaning; no referent is replaced, narrowed, or broadened.
strongest_objection: One might claim the book’s brief phrasing under-emphasizes pure idolatry relative to political kingdoms, yet the printed citations and wording still cover both without contradiction.
